subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core expand `update.auto` into a first-class scheduled approval and notification workflow, and which parts should stay in core versus Control UI, chat commands, rollback/safe-update work, or external updater architecture?
rationale: The request defines new public config and unattended update behavior in a security-sensitive core workflow, so automation should not choose the approval, notification, persistence, or scope boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep as core workflow tracker
options.body: Use this issue to design the schedule, confirm/notify-only, safe channel delivery, and post-restart reporting behavior on the supervised update path.

options.title: Split to narrower tracks
options.body: Keep only the engine requirements here and route UI discoverability, chat `/update`, rollback, plugin updates, and HTTP update authority to their existing related issues.

options.title: Decline built-in workflow
options.body: Keep the current package auto-updater and document cron, agent, or external operator automation as the supported advanced path.

recommendation.title: Keep as core workflow tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the schedule, confirm/notify-only, safe channel delivery, and post-restart reporting behavior on the supervised update path.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced the current core auto-updater and has the strongest product/history signal for the remaining workflow boundary.
